articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Because apparently even Patch Tuesday needs steroids now.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military hackers turned ancient router vulnerabilities into Microsoft Office token harvesting machines. Your router from 2015 is basically a gift that keeps on giving—to the FSB.

articles.title: Yet Another Way to Bypass Google Chrome's Encryption Protection
articles.summary: NSA whistleblower William Binney's warning about 'turnkey totalitarian state' surveillance infrastructure remains as chilling and relevant as ever. The architecture of oppression is ready and waiting.

articles.title: Instructure Breach Exposes Schools' Vendor Dependence
articles.summary: VoidStealer Trojan authors found yet another way to bypass Google Chrome's App-Bound Encryption. Chrome's security is apparently more like suggestions than actual walls.

articles.title: From Stuxnet to ChatGPT: 20 News Events That Shaped Cyber
articles.summary: ShinyHunters breached Instructure's Canvas LMS, exposing how educational institutions put blind trust in vendors. Schools got schooled on third-party risk management.

articles.title: India orders infosec red alert in case Mythos sparks crime spree
articles.summary: UK's age-gating plans threaten to break the internet while completely missing the point about Big Tech's surveillance capitalism. Another brilliant solution that solves nothing.

articles.title: The Hacker News Launches 'Cybersecurity Stars Awards 2026' — Submissions Now Open
articles.summary: Iranian MuddyWater group uses Microsoft Teams for credential theft in false flag ransomware ops. When state-sponsored hackers start LARPing as ransomware gangs, you know the attribution game is broken.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: AI-Powered Phishing, Android Spying Tool, Linux Exploit, GitHub RCE & More
articles.summary: Instructure hacker claims 280 million student and staff records stolen from 8,809 educational institutions. When your LMS becomes a data exfiltration platform, maybe it's time to rethink EdTech security.

articles.title: 15-year-old detained over massive data breach at French government agency
articles.summary: 2026 declared the year of AI-assisted attacks, with Japanese teen arrested for breaching 7 million Kaikatsu Club records. The kids are definitely not alright—they're getting scarier.

articles.title: Attackers are cashing in on fresh 'CopyFail' Linux flaw
articles.summary: 15-year-old detained for breaching French government agency, compromising up to 18 million records from France Titres. Teenage hackers are making government cybersecurity look like amateur hour.
